newsitem.title: UK: Ladbroke gains as Hilton bid talk grows.
newsitem.headline: Ladbroke gains as Hilton bid talk grows.

text.p: Shares in Ladbroke Group Plc advanced on Thursday as speculation that Hilton Hotels Corp will be more likely to bid for the company if its hostile bid for ITT Corp fails, dealers and analysts said.
The stock put on 2-1/2p to 271p having hit 278p.
Today's bid talk was sparked by Wednesday's news that ITT plans a massive restructuring to thwart the $6.5 billion Hilton bid.
"Hilton is after ITT's Sheraton hotels and if the deal falls through its attention may turn to Ladbroke with which it already has a strategic alliance," said one special salesman.

The alliance, sealed early this year, allows each company to take a stake of up to 20 percent in the other and Hilton Hotels has already said it intends to acquire a five percent stake in Ladbroke in due course.
"This (the new ITT defensive move) certainly makes Hilton acquiring that five percent stake in Ladbroke more likely," said the special salesman.
Ladbroke stock was also helped today by a "buy" note as debut coverage from Credit Lyonnais Laing.

The note by analyst Mark Brumby said Ladbroke was the best stock in a dull sector. Brumby said the share price had more mileage, hotel occupancies were up and getting better, there was more profitability from a reorganisation of its betting and gaming units and better margins from new scratch cards business where the effect of Britain's National Lottery has faded, dealers said.
Brumby was not immediately available to comment.
